title: Coordinated tenant throttling and connection-shed strategy for Hosted API 5xx/timeouts during escalations
creator: Asha Patel
description: During a multi-tenant capacity surge on hosted inference in late Feb, we observed clustered 5xx errors and elevated timeouts affecting high-volume tenants and small tenants alike. This ticket captures design and implementation of a coordinated throttling and connection-shed strategy to keep the fleet healthy during escalations while preserving fairness and minimizing customer-visible errors.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate tenant burst: open 2k concurrent requests to /v1/generate for tenant A with long_seq=2048 over a 60s window.
2) Introduce mixed traffic from 20 other tenants with random short requests to create resource contention.
3) Observe connection pool exhaustion in the frontend, increased queue time in serving runtime, and 502/504s from downstream NGINX/proxy due to overloaded worker threads.
4) Re-run with SDK default retry behavior (exponential, 3 retries) to observe amplification effect on load.
5) Validate logs and traces via hosted-reliability dashboard to confirm correlation between queue depth and 5xx spike.
proposed_solution: 1) Implement tenant-priority queues in proxy that enforce per-tenant in-flight limits and soft tokens that can be reduced when total queue depth exceeds threshold.
2) Add coordinated shed signal from runtime to proxy: an /internal/shed endpoint that reports worker queue_percentile; proxy applies global backpressure policy when percentile>85%.
3) Introduce a short-term lightweight model fallback path (compatible lower-cost variant) for heavy tenants when latency SLOs are at risk.
4) Align SDK retry semantics: return 429 to clients when shedding is active and include Retry-After, plus publish SDK patch to switch to jittered linear retries when server-sent Retry-After exists.
5) Add a kill-switch feature flag to turn coordinated-shed on/off per-region/stack for progressive rollout.
6) Expand observability: per-tenant queue depth, inflight token usage, and shed state exported to console and alerting rules.
mitigation_history: 2025-02-21: Emergency mitigation - increased proxy worker threads, rolled temporary tenant-level rate caps for top 5 noisy tenants (manual). Reduced immediate error rate by ~40%.
2025-02-24: Hotfix deployed - tightened SDK client timeouts and aligned backend idle connection reuse. Short-term latency improved but 5xx waves recurred under sustained bursts.
2025-02-27: Per-tenant circuit breaker enabled (soft) with 30s cooldown; identified two tenants with pathological retry patterns. Communication sent to both customers via CSM.
2025-03-02: Began dev work on coordinated-shed prototype (spike ENG-88122-SPIKE).
pr_links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/3092 - initial shed endpoint and per-tenant token buckets
https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/124 - SDK Retry-After handling and jittered linear fallback
acceptance_criteria: 1) Under synthetic burst tests (as in steps_to_reproduce) system maintains <2% 5xx rate and latency P95 below SLO for non-noisy tenants.
2) Coordinated-shed can be toggled by region and rollout via feature flag with no downtime.
3) SDK patch published and clients receive Retry-After header during shedding; integration tests validate reduced retry amplification.
4) Console surfaces per-tenant shed state and token usage; alert fires when shed is active for >1 minute for >5% of tenants.
5) No regression in Dedicated/private stacks (smoke tests pass) - ensure feature gate off for Private by default.
notes: Trade-offs considered: immediate aggressive tenant hard-capping reduces errors fastest but risks breaking low-latency interactive workloads; opted for soft tokens + graceful fallback to reduce customer-visible failures.
We intentionally avoid blackholing traffic; preference for 429+Retry-After so clients can back off explicitly.
Coordination between proxy and runtime adds coupling but gives the most targeted leverage points to protect worker pools without global throttles.
